ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the diagram, each of the squares touches adjacent squares at its corners and the line $GH$ along one of its edges. The line $GH$ is $24\mathrm{~cm}$ long. What is the total perimeter, in centimetres, of all the squares?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a horizontal line segment GH, and several gray squares are arranged from left to right along this line; some squares are above the line, and some are below the line. Each square has one entire side attached to GH, and adjacent squares meet at corner points, so their sides attached to GH are connected end to end in sequence. Reasoning: Let the side lengths of these squares from left to right be s1, s2, ..., sk. Because their sides on GH exactly form the entire segment GH, s1 + s2 + ... + sk = 24. The total sum of the perimeters of all the squares is 4s1 + 4s2 + ... + 4sk = 4(s1 + s2 + ... + sk) = 4 × 24 = 96. Therefore the total perimeter is 96 centimeters.

raw_record.question_text: In the diagram, each of the squares touches adjacent squares at its corners and the line $GH$ along one of its edges. The line $GH$ is $24\mathrm{~cm}$ long. What is the total perimeter, in centimetres, of all the squares?

method.method_draft: Read the diagram from left to right: there are several squares, each having one full side lying on the horizontal segment GH, and adjacent squares meet exactly at corners, so their sides on GH are consecutive with no overlaps or gaps between G and H. Let the side lengths of the squares be s1, s2, ..., sk in left-to-right order. From the image structure and the text condition, GH = s1 + s2 + ... + sk = 24. The total perimeter of all squares is 4s1 + 4s2 + ... + 4sk = 4(s1 + ... + sk) = 4 · 24 = 96.

method.method_draft: Group the perimeter edges by corresponding edge position rather than naming individual square sizes. From the diagram, one edge of every square lies on GH; because adjacent squares touch at corners, these GH-edges together make the full 24 cm segment. Since every square has four equal edges, if you take the 'GH edge' from each square, their total length is 24; the matching opposite edges have the same total length 24, and the two sets of perpendicular side edges also each total 24. Thus the total perimeter is four equal copies of the combined GH-edge length: 24 + 24 + 24 + 24 = 96.
